Approve H for the lifecycle change from B in ReportReader.java:40–45. No supported blocking or non-blocking defects were identified in this scope.

At ReportReader.java:41, try (session) enforces the accepted ownership contract: ReportReader owns the session on entry and must close it on success or failure. B omitted that cleanup; H supplies it while leaving the correct mapping unchanged. The author's leak-fix claim is supported by this contract and the supplied H test reports, rather than by the syntax alone.

The production path also supports the change. ExportJob.java:18 acquires s and line 19 transfers ownership to reader.read(s). The caller neither reuses nor closes s afterward. Its line 20 audit uses an independent auditSink, so invalidating s does not create a use-after-close defect in that audit operation.

The second reviewer's exception-replacement allegation is incorrect under the supplied Java rule. When the body and close() both throw, the body exception remains primary and the close exception is suppressed on it. When the body succeeds and close() throws, the close exception propagates instead of returning rows. That behavior is not a demonstrated contract violation here.

Validation is limited to the authoritative supplied facts and reports. The reported H tests cover correct rows and one close on success and repository failure; they do not exercise ExportJob or establish throwing-close coverage. I ran no tests and inspected no repository implementation. Caller compatibility and exception precedence are therefore static conclusions from the supplied contract, caller facts, and language rule.
